q1_issues.issue: "a small heap of silken threads" is encoded with (CardinalityPhrase sk_threads_1 "heap"), a phrase outside the instruction set's vague-quantity lexicon, and it drops the collective-noun typing (Member <g> heap) that the "a flock of birds" pattern requires, leaving "small" predicated of a group typed only as silken_thread.

The bare mass kind symbol weak_mist_light is used directly as the Agent role filler of a generic present-tense clause, where the instruction set routes a verbal generic over a kind through a distributing Implication rule (sealed as a conjunct) rather than a flat event on the kind symbol.

q2_gaps: Container / quantity partitives ("a small heap of silken threads", "a cup of water"): named as excluded from the genitive rules but given no encoding of their own, and "heap" is not in the vague-quantity lexicon.

A bare mass-noun subject of a generic verbal clause ("weak mist-light attracts a handful of nightmoths"): the generic-rule machinery ranges over instances via (Member $x kind), which does not fit a mass kind, and nothing licenses a bare kind symbol as a subject role filler.

Cross-seal coreference: a definite inside one seal re-mentioning an indefinite witness introduced inside an earlier seal ("a dim lantern" ... "the lantern"), and whether the definite-projection rule then lets that witness's typing reach top level even though its existence was deliberately withheld by the first seal.
notes: Seal discipline is otherwise clean: no predication of any reported proposition reaches top level, and only definite-referent typing plus compound-decomposition Inheritance atoms project. The tell/write attitude events, the Experiencer/Recipient assignment, the tenseless generic complements, the unfused "dim lantern", and the collective four-Agent "form a closed loop" event all follow the instruction set.
